column1: # Control set: PQQ-dependent alcohol dehydrogenases (methanol/ethanol family) whose
# metal cofactor is known from the primary literature. Used by src/validate_classifier.jl
# to test whether the D-x-D rule, read at the calibrated active-site column, recovers the
# cofactor that experiment reports.
# Every row is a factual claim about a published enzyme. The accession, organism, PDB id
# and metal of each row were checked against the cited paper, the UniProt entry and the
# PDB entry before the row was written. Rows without a direct measurement are not thrown
# away: they are placed in a weaker tier so that they can be scored apart.
# role
#   reference  Sequences the pipeline calibrates on. They locate the active-site column
#              and never enter a held-out stratum, so they cannot flatter one; they are
#              reported apart, in a stratum of their own. Which
#              two of them calibrate a run is passed to validate() as ln_ref_acc and
#              ca_ref_acc; it is not read from this file.
#   test       Held out. Only rows with role = test enter an accuracy.
# tier, strongest evidence first
#   ref  A reference row (see above). Belongs to no held-out stratum.
#   A    Direct determination for this protein: the metal resolved in a crystal structure
#        of the enzyme itself, or measured in (or required by) the purified enzyme.
#   B    Indirect but gene specific: expression, deletion mutant or growth evidence ties
#        this gene to a Ca- or Ln-dependent activity, but no metal was measured in,
#        reconstituted into or shown to be required by the purified enzyme, or the enzyme
#        was not purified at all.
#   C    Homology only. The cofactor is inherited from close relatives and was never
#        measured for this protein. Kept as a separate stratum.
#   X    Contested. Reported together with its call and excluded from every accuracy.
# cofactor  Lanthanide | Calcium   (the Symbol values the pipeline emits)
# domain    Bacteria on every row; the set contains no archaeal enzyme.
# evidence  One line on why the cofactor is considered known for this protein.
# citation  Author year of the work the evidence comes from and, where no published work
#           covers the row's own strain, the sequence record the row rests on.
# pdb       Structures holding that metal, semicolon separated. Blank when there is none.
# source    Provenance of the row: manual (pinned by hand from the cited papers),
#           robinson2026 (adopted from Robinson et al. 2026 Table S4), ncbi (the sequence
#           is fetched from the NCBI protein record; its UniProtKB entry D5MI89 was
#           deleted, so there is no active accession to fetch).
# Deleted UniProtKB entries keep their accession here, and the fetcher rescues the sequence
# from UniParc and names the UniParc id in the evidence cell. The one exception is the
# source = ncbi row, which carries the NCBI protein accession instead (see source above).
# THIRD-PARTY SOURCE OF THE source = robinson2026 ROWS
#   Robinson CM, Martinez-Gomez NC, West-Roberts J, Voutsinos M, Banfield JF.
#   "Evidence for lanthanide and PQQ dependent dehydrogenases in Eukarya."
#   Supplementary tables:  https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.32981990.v1
#   Licence:               CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)
# What was taken from Table S4 and what was not. Taken: the accession, the organism, the
# calcium cofactor, the fact that the determination is inferred rather than direct, and a
# short author-year for the underlying work where that work covers the row's own strain.
# For Q9L935 it does not, so that row cites the GenBank sequence record the entry rests on
# instead, and its evidence cell says why. NOT taken: that table's own reference
# strings, its motif calls, and its coordinating-oxygen counts. Every evidence cell in
# this file is written here, not copied. The rows are a small factual extraction, checked
# against the cited papers and the UniProt entries before they were written, and they are
# marked source = robinson2026 so that they can be dropped or re-derived as a block.
# LICENCE OF THIS FILE. The compilation is covered by this repository's MIT licence (see
# LICENSE). That does not replace the citations the rows carry: if you reuse the table,
# carry them with it, and carry the attribution above with the robinson2026 rows.
